top_choice_rationale: P001 (Kiyotaki and Moore, B002) is a close call over P002 on merit, and I rank it first mainly on attribution. The 1997 paper is a two-author origin of a distinct mechanism: borrowing limits tied to collateral values feed back on asset prices, so temporary shocks become persistent and amplified. It has nearly three decades of use in macro-finance, quantitative macro and policy modelling, and a two-name citation leaves out nobody who wrote the founding paper. P002 (Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn, B012) is nearly as strong on originality, maturity and reach. However, Bresnahan, Benkard and Levin are credited on the same ballot, and a three-person cap cannot cover them. I do not treat that omission as fixable by wording. Open risks for P001 are overlap with the 2022 prize and the weak identification of aggregate amplification. I read the overlap as thematic, since that prize concerned banks and runs. The micro evidence I recall supports the channel but not its size, and I have not verified it. I rank P002 above no award because it is a mature, defensible achievement. P000 is last because two awards are scientifically defensible.
